summary: Worked example (live, owner-supervised, 2026-11-28) — the first full grant cycle run under GRANT_APPLICATION_PLAYBOOK.md, captured as a lesson per CONTINUOUS_LEARNING_AND_GROWTH.md. WHAT WAS DONE: four grant applications for Interplanetary Fund were researched, field-mapped, and filled to the owner-only step, with the deadline — Monday November 30, 2026, 11:59pm ET — verified on each funder's own page: Amber Grant (WomensNet), IFundWomen Startup Accelerator Grant, Hey Helen Grant (Visionaries), and HerRise MicroGrant (HerSuiteSpot). No application was submitted and no fee was paid; every form stopped exactly where the owner's own act was required. LESSONS: (1) Map fields from the verified Business Information Register before drafting anything — legal name, entity form (Washington sole proprietorship), registration date (October 2, 2026), address, and contact details came from the register, not from memory, and no field was filled from a guess. (2) Draft narrative answers from verified facts only: woman-owned Washington sole proprietorship, registered October 2, 2026, live AI-powered fundraising platform, pre-revenue, bootstrapped and self-funded — no invented revenue, user counts, or projections. (3) Identify the owner-only steps at the START of each form and never cross them: the rules-attestation click (IFundWomen's 'I accept'), signature and fee-acknowledgment radios (Hey Helen), and fee-consent checkboxes and card entry (HerRise, Amber) all belong to the owner; preparation stops there and hands over cleanly. (4) The always-waive rule ran in the same pass — every fee in the cycle was met with a waiver request first (companion lesson: department correspondence, topic fee-waiver-emails). (5) A form with no save function is a trap: the Amber form holds its draft only while its tab stays open, so it is never navigated away from mid-cycle. (6) Missing required data is escalated, never guessed: Hey Helen's required household-income bracket had no truthful source on file, so it was left unselected and put to the owner as an open question. APPLICATION: this lesson improves GRANT_APPLICATION_PLAYBOOK.md — the live run confirms the playbook's map-fields-then-fill order, STOP gates, and gap-list discipline held in practice; candidate revisions come from the outcome review once the funders respond. Filed unverified by design: it records owner-observed work, not a checked external source.
title: Worked example 2026-11-28 — four grant applications filled to the owner-only step (Amber, IFundWomen, Hey Helen, HerRise)
